title: Scheduler coalescing regression — P0 hosted API outage (2027-08-05)
content:
Summary:
On 2027-08-05 02:13 UTC we observed a P0 outage affecting the hosted API. Symptoms included sudden tail-latency spikes for both streaming and non-streaming requests and a correlated increase in 5xx errors (predominantly 502/504). The failure window lasted ~1h 22m with elevated customer impact until mitigation completed. Root cause: a regression in the request coalescing logic in the front-end scheduler introduced a race that caused resource starvation in the per-instance worker pool under certain request mix conditions. The regression shipped as part of a rollout (serving-runtime v1.12.0) earlier that day.

Impact:
- Regions affected: us-west-2 and us-east-1 (traffic routed to these regions experienced most failures); other regions saw elevated latencies but not full failures due to routing fallbacks.
- Customer-facing: ~9% of requests in affected regions returned 5xx during the peak; median latency stayed within SLO but p95/p99 increased by 3–15x depending on model and sequence length.
- Streaming: ~12% of streaming sessions experienced repeated stream resets or long stalls leading to reconnections.
- Business: High alert volume, several customers filed support tickets for degraded UX. No data loss.

Detection and Triage:
- First alert: automated p99 latency alert fired for hosted-api-per-route in us-west-2 at 02:13 UTC. SRE on-call (Ethan) triaged and saw simultaneous 502 surge in ingestion plane.
- Quick checks: infra dashboards, ingress error distributions, per-instance CPU and threadpool metrics. Notable findings: increased queue depth on the front-end scheduler, thread count saturation in the worker pool, and abrupt drop in successful upstream connections.
- Incident call established at 02:21 UTC (slack channel #sre-incident-2027-08-05).

Mitigation timeline:
- 02:25 UTC: Rollback of serving-runtime v1.12.0 to v1.11.7 in us-west-2 (canary rollout had completed earlier that day). Immediate drop in 5xx rate in the canary subset.
- 02:37 UTC: Automated routing rules adjusted to shift 60% of us-west-2 traffic to us-east-1 to reduce load on affected fleet while full rollback completed.
- 03:05 UTC: Full rollback in us-west-2 finished; 5xxs declined to baseline but p99 latencies remained elevated as worker pools drained.
- 03:38 UTC: Identified that us-east-1 also showed the same pattern once rollouts reached larger cohorts; rollback initiated there and completed by 03:55 UTC.
- 04:00–04:35 UTC: Backpressure and retry storms caused intermittent secondary spikes; SRE throttled client retries at the edge and enabled a temporary circuit-breaker to reduce cascading contention.
- 04:36 UTC: Service returned to acceptable SLOs for most routes. Monitoring remained under watch for 2 hours.

Root cause analysis (why this happened):
1) Code change: A refactor to the scheduler coalescing heuristic (PR #1984) intended to improve batching for low-latency short sequences introduced a subtle ordering change in the scheduler's lock acquisition. Under mixed workload (long streaming sessions + short synchronous requests), a race could occur where the coalescing thread held a spinlock while waiting on I/O, preventing worker assignment and causing the worker pool to deplete.
2) Failure mode: When workers got starved, incoming requests were queued; the front-end hit connection timeouts and returned 502/504. Streaming sessions, which rely on steady KV cache and streaming pump threads, observed stalls and reconnects.
3) Rollout exposure: Canary criteria were too permissive for this change. The canary traffic mix did not include production-level long-lived streaming sessions, so the regression was not observed during canary. The change was then promoted to production fleets where the mixed workload exposed the race.
4) Observability gaps: Metrics that would have signaled the race earlier (per-instance lock contention, worker pool starvation ratio, coalescing wait time histogram) were either not instrumented or not part of standard dashboards/alerts.

Contributing factors:
- Insufficient canary traffic diversity (no streaming-heavy canary).
- Missing telemetry around scheduler internal waits and lock contention.
- Rollout automation lacked an automated rollback trigger tied to worker-pool exhaustion metrics.

Corrective actions (short-term) — done during incident:
- Immediate rollback of the v1.12.0 change in affected regions (owner: release-eng, completed 03:55 UTC).
- Temporary client-side retry throttling at edge proxy to dampen retry storms (owner: sre, implemented 04:10 UTC).
- Emergency circuit-breaker put in front of streaming pump allocation for new sessions to limit concurrent new streaming sessions while workers recovered (owner: serving-runtime oncall).

Corrective actions (medium and long-term):
1) Patch and fix the root cause: revert ordering change and add a safe non-blocking coalescing path that yields during I/O (owner: serving-runtime team, PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1999). Target: 2027-08-12.
2) Add deterministic unit/integration tests that simulate mixed workloads (short sync + long streaming sessions) to catch this class of race (owner: applied-ml + serving-runtime). Target: 2027-08-19.
3) Instrumentation: add metrics for lock contention, coalescing wait histograms, worker-starvation ratio, and expose them on the standard SRE dashboards (owner: observability team). Target: 2027-08-15.
4) Canary policy update: update canary traffic profile to include a configurable % of long-lived streaming sessions and higher concurrency scenarios; add automated guard rails to pause rollouts on anomalous worker-pool metrics (owner: release-engineering). Target: 2027-08-10.
5) Rollout automation: implement an automated rollback when worker pool starvation or per-instance queue depth exceeds thresholds for N minutes (owner: platform-engineering). Target: 2027-08-17.
6) Runbook updates: update hosted-api incident runbook to include checklist for scheduler/worker starvation signals and the steps for temporary circuit-breaker and client throttling (owner: eng-sre). Target: 2027-08-09.
7) Post-incident customer communication: coordinate with customer-success to send an incident summary to impacted customers with timeline and mitigation details (owner: customer-success). Target: 2027-08-09.

Learnings and recommendations:
- Canary traffic needs to mirror real production workload shapes. A/B canaries must include synthetic long-lived streaming sessions to surface scheduling races.
- Small changes to lock acquisition ordering can have outsized effects in high-concurrency runtimes; prefer lock-free or yield-friendly designs where possible.
- Invest early in exposing internal runtime metrics (contention, wait times) — these are critical for observing emergent behavior before alerts trigger customer-visible SLO breaches.

Action items (table-like list):
- Fix and merge safe coalescing path (owner: Priya Kapoor, target: 2027-08-12). Linked PR: PR #1999.
- Add integration test harness for mixed workloads (owner: Luis Hernandez, target: 2027-08-19). Jira: SRE-5460.
- Instrument scheduler internals and add dashboards/alerts (owner: Jing Wei, target: 2027-08-15). Jira: SRE-5459.
- Update canary policy and rollout guards (owner: Release-ENG Lead, target: 2027-08-10). Jira: REL-312.
- Update incident runbook (owner: Samira Patel, target: 2027-08-09).

Postmortem review:
- This doc reviewed in SRE weekly postmortem readout on 2027-08-07. Action owners assigned and dates agreed.

Appendix (notes from on-call):
- Observed spike in scheduler wait time histogram at 02:14 UTC concurrent with a spike in per-instance epoll_wait backlog.
- Heap/CPU were normal; this was not a memory leak but scheduling contention.
- Client retry patterns: several SDK clients retried at aggressive backoff settings (0ms jitter) causing localized retry storms after initial 502s — we recommended client SDK update to exponential backoff with jitter.
- Retro note: put a small manual gating step for runtime refactors that touch scheduler semantics next to rollout automation until tests and telemetry are in place.

If there are questions or missing details, reach out in slack:#sre-incident-2027-08-05 or email samira.patel@redwood-inference.com.
